question: When the sandbox dies mid-review, or a round follows earlier Kody suggestions on the same PR, does what reaches the PR match what a correct review delivers — nothing unread, revisions linked, nothing already sent posted again?

cases.checks: Kody Rule on a test assertion that casts with `as unknown as` instead of comparing with plain null; the developer rewrote the line and kept the cast; stored implemented; 1 earlier comment
Kody Rule requiring a justification comment on partial fixtures (RSpec); the developer answered with a "# fixture" label that justifies nothing; stored not_implemented; 1 earlier comment
Bug finder; an event poller reads only the first page and moves its cursor past the rest; the developer raised the page size but still reads one page; stored implemented; 2 earlier comments
Finder: the earlier security comment flagged one output sink that did not strip inline markup (implemented); the diff adds two new sinks without the stripping; 2 earlier comments

delivered.text:
**Revises an earlier Kody suggestion** on `src/jobs/handler.ts:5` (2026-09-30 00:46 UTC).

The current ordering stores the result at line 5 before updating progress at line 6, so a crash in between leaves a stored result for a job whose progress was never marked, violating Rule [1]'s requirement that `db.progress.update` run before `db.results.insert` in the same job handler. Call `db.progress.update` first, then `db.results.insert`.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The new `log.warn('retrying', { attempt })` at line 11 (and the `sleep` call) execute on every catch, including the final iteration where `attempt === attempts` and no retry follows. WHY: When the last attempt fails, the loop exits and throws `lastError`, but a misleading "retrying" log was emitted and a needless backoff timer scheduled for a retry that never happens — operators see a retry event that did not occur. HOW: Only log/sleep when another attempt will actually run, e.g. `if (attempt < attempts) { log.warn('retrying', { attempt }); await sleep(200 * attempt); }`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim is factually accurate. In the loop at src/sync/retry.ts:6-14, on the final iteration (attempt === attempts) a failure still executes `log.warn('retrying', { attempt })` and `sleep(200 * attempt)` before the loop exits and throws lastError at line 15. So a 'retrying' log is emitted and a backoff timer is scheduled even though no further attempt will run — a misleading log/needless timer, exactly as described. Note: `sleep` is not awaited here (line 12), which is a separate issue already covered by PreviousDecision round-a-await-sleep; this finding targets the misleading final-iteration log/sleep, a different consequence, so it is not a repeat. The finding is a real behavioral bug, not merely style.

delivered.label: bug
delivered.text: On the final iteration where `attempt === attempts`, the `log.warn('retrying', { attempt })` at line 11 and the `sleep` call still execute, so operators see a retry event that never occurs and a needless backoff timer is scheduled before the loop throws `lastError`. Guard both with `if (attempt < attempts)` so they only run when another attempt will actually happen.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: `sleep(200 * attempt)` is executed on every failed attempt including the last one, so when all attempts are exhausted the function sleeps before throwing instead of returning immediately. WHY: with attempts=3 a fully failing sync now blocks an extra 600ms after the third failure before surfacing the error, delaying the caller for no benefit since no retry will follow. HOW: skip the backoff on the final attempt, e.g. `if (attempt < attempts) sleep(200 * attempt);`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: the catch block at line 12 calls sleep(200 * attempt) unconditionally on every failed attempt, including the final iteration (attempt === attempts). After the loop exhausts, line 15 throws lastError — but only after the last sleep has run, so a fully failing 3-attempt sync adds 200+400+600 = 1200ms of blocking, of which the final 600ms delays the error with no retry following. The finding's claim is factually accurate about the code path. This is a distinct issue from PreviousDecision round-a-await-sleep, which addressed the missing await on sleep(200); that decision changed the sleep value to 200*attempt but did not eliminate the pointless final-attempt backoff, so this is a new/different problem (unnecessary delay on the last attempt), not a repeat of the 'sleep not awaited' failure.

delivered.label: bug

Guard it with `if (attempt < attempts)` and `await` the `sleep(200 * attempt)` call so the delay only happens when another attempt is coming.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: `sleep(200 * attempt)` is called without `await` (and without `return`), so the returned Promise is never waited on before the loop proceeds to the next attempt. WHY: `sleep` is `(ms) => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms))` (src/sync/sleep.ts:1); dropping the `await` means the backoff never elapses and a failing service is retried `attempts` times back-to-back with no delay — the retry/backoff this commit claims to add does not take effect. HOW: await the sleep: `await sleep(200 * attempt);`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The technical claim is accurate (sleep at line 12 is not awaited, so no backoff elapses), but this is verbatim the same problem already raised on this PR by PreviousDecision round-a-await-sleep (src/sync/retry.ts:10): "withRetry calls sleep(200) without await... Await the sleep." Same operation, same failure (retries fire back-to-back with no delay). It is a repeat of an already-posted review comment and must be dropped.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the newly added backoff call `sleep(200 * attempt)` is not awaited, so it schedules a timer and returns immediately instead of pausing the loop. WHY: every retry still fires back-to-back against the failing dependency — the same lost-backoff failure the earlier review flagged — because `sleep` (src/sync/sleep.ts:1) is an async function whose promise is discarded here. HOW: `await sleep(200 * attempt);` inside the catch block.
verificationEvidence.rationale: This is the same problem already raised in PreviousReviewDecisions entry round-a-await-sleep: 'withRetry calls sleep(200) without await, so every retry fires immediately after the failure and the backoff never happens... Await the sleep.' The current code at line 12 is `sleep(200 * attempt);` — still un-awaited, just with the argument scaled by attempt. The failure is identical (lost backoff / back-to-back retries) in the same operation (withRetry's catch block), so it is a repeat of that entry regardless of the tweaked argument, and the decision was already posted on this PR. Per the rules, drop it.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: handleEvent is awaited inside the loop with no error handling, so any rejection from invoices.markPaid/markVoided/markPastDue aborts pollOnce before cursors.set(CURSOR_KEY, pollStartedAt) runs. WHY: the cursor never advances, so the next tick re-reads the identical window and replays every already-processed event; a single event whose handler deterministically throws permanently wedges the poller (all later events are starved) and repeatedly re-applies the prefix. HOW: isolate each event so one failure cannot block cursor advancement, e.g. wrap the handleEvent call in try/catch (log and continue), or record the last successfully processed event id and set the cursor to it in a finally block.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: line 13 awaits handleEvent with no error isolation, so any rejection from markPaid/markVoided/markPastDue throws out of pollOnce before cursors.set(CURSOR_KEY, pollStartedAt) at line 17 executes. The cursor then never advances, so the next tick re-reads the identical window and replays processed events; a deterministically-throwing event permanently wedges the poller. This is a distinct failure from PreviousDecision index 1 (which was about pagination loss / only the first page being read), so it is not a repeat — different root cause and different consequence. Not refutable from the code.

delivered.label: bug
delivered.text: In `src/billing/poller.ts`, awaiting `handleEvent` inside the loop without error handling means any rejection from `invoices.markPaid`/`markVoided`/`markPastDue` aborts `pollOnce` before `cursors.set(CURSOR_KEY, pollStartedAt)` runs, so the cursor never advances and the next tick re-reads the identical window, replaying every processed event; a deterministically throwing event permanently wedges the poller and starves all later events. Isolate each event so one failure cannot block cursor advancement, e.g. wrap the `handleEvent` call in `try`/`catch` to log and continue, or record the last successfully processed event id and set the cursor to it in a `finally` block.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: pollOnce reads only one page and then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt, while the comment at lines 15-16 falsely asserts that with PAGE_SIZE=500 `page.hasMore` is never true. WHY: the EventsClient contract (events-client.ts:16-17) states the provider caps limit at 100, so limit:500 still returns at most 100 events and hasMore/nextCursor remain meaningful; whenever more than 100 events exist since the stored cursor, the rest are never fetched and the cursor jumps past them, permanently losing invoice.paid/voided/payment_failed events (invoices never marked paid/voided/past-due). HOW: follow nextCursor until hasMore is false before advancing the cursor, e.g. `let cursor: string | undefined; let page; do { page = await client.listEvents({ createdAfter: since, createdBefore: pollStartedAt, limit: PAGE_SIZE, cursor }); for (const event of page.data) await handleEvent(invoices, event); cursor = page.nextCursor ?? undefined; } while (page.hasMore);` then `await cursors.set(CURSOR_KEY, pollStartedAt);`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The candidate describes the exact same failure as PreviousDecision index 1 (round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only): pollOnce reads one page, then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt, losing invoice events when more than one page exists. It only re-attributes the cause (provider caps limit at 100, so PAGE_SIZE=500 still returns ≤100 and hasMore stays true). The failure — same data loss in the same operation at the same location — is a repeat of the already-posted suggestion, so it must be dropped regardless of the entry's Outcome or the new cause named.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: pollOnce still reads only one page and then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt; the new comment claims `page.hasMore is never true` because PAGE_SIZE=500, but EventsClient.listEvents documents (events-client.ts:16) that the provider caps limit at 100, so a 500 limit still returns at most 100 events. WHY: when more than 100 events exist in the [since, pollStartedAt) window, page.hasMore is true and page.nextCursor points to the remainder; pollOnce ignores both and moves the cursor to pollStartedAt, so the unread invoice events are skipped forever (invoices never marked paid/voided/past due). HOW: follow the cursor — loop while page.hasMore, passing page.nextCursor as `cursor`, and only then set the cursor to pollStartedAt; the PAGE_SIZE comment should be removed since it does not raise the effective page size.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The candidate's failure — pollOnce reads a single page, then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt, so when page.hasMore is true the remaining events are never read and invoice events are lost — is exactly the failure PreviousReviewDecisions entry round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only already raised on this same PR (same file, same lines, same fix: follow page.nextCursor until hasMore is false before advancing the cursor). Per the instructions, re-raising the problem an entry already raised is a DROP, even when it blames a new cause (the provider capping limit at 100 vs PAGE_SIZE=500) and even though the comment now claims hasMore is never true — that is a new justification, not a new failure. The entry's Outcome is "implemented"; the current diff only shows a comment claiming the bug cannot happen, with no concrete evidence the applied fix was reverted. Same crash/data-loss in the same operation = repeat.

WHY: a commenter can post a body containing (mass-ping) or which renders as a live link in chat, and raw HTML in the inbox item is rendered as is (clients.ts:11), giving stored HTML/markup injection. HOW: wrap both values with stripInlineMarkup as mentionEmail already does, e.g. text: `${stripInlineMarkup(m.authorName)} mentioned you: ${stripInlineMarkup(m.body)}` and html: `${stripInlineMarkup(m.authorName)} mentioned you: ${stripInlineMarkup(m.body)}`.

delivered.text: `ChatClient.post` renders `text` as chat markup, so a comment containing `<https://evil.example|Reset password>` becomes a live link in a message sent from our bot and `<!channel>` pings the whole channel — a ready phishing and abuse vector. Wrap both `m.authorName` and `m.body` in `stripInlineMarkup`, matching the sibling `mentionEmail` and the `sanitize.ts` contract that every outbound sink sanitizes user text.
